title: Multiply Your Business: New Marketing Realities to Catapult Your Income
author: Gerry Robert
summary:
*Multiply Your Business* is Gerry Robert's marketing-focused follow-up to his earlier bestseller *The Millionaire Mindset*, aimed at small-business owners and entrepreneurs whose core expertise lies outside marketing but who need practical, low-cost strategies to attract customers in a changed marketplace. The book's central premise, drawn from reader and review descriptions, is that many businesses continue relying on outdated marketing assumptions from an earlier commercial era, and that a handful of specific, current strategic shifts — Robert frames them as roughly a dozen "new marketing realities" — separate businesses that grow from those that plateau or decline despite offering a genuinely good product or service.

A central strategy running through the book, according to available reviews of the work, is the use of writing and publishing a book as a marketing and branding tool in its own right — creating credibility, differentiation, and inbound interest that competing on price or generic advertising cannot easily replicate. This reflects Robert's own career path: after building publishing ventures specifically oriented toward helping entrepreneurs use authorship as a business-growth tool, he treats the book-as-marketing-asset idea as one of the more emphasized "realities" in the text, alongside the general instruction that a business's central challenge is usually a marketing challenge, not a product-quality challenge.

Because I was not able to verify a specific, edition-confirmed list of all the individual "new marketing realities" covered, the entry below is intentionally more conservative on granular chapter-by-chapter claims than for the other books in this batch — the whole-book summary, key lessons, and Apply This sections reflect the strategies I could confirm with reasonable confidence from available descriptions of the book (the book-as-marketing-tool strategy specifically, plus the book's general framing around outdated versus current marketing assumptions), rather than inventing detail for the remaining unconfirmed realities.

The overall tone, consistent with Robert's broader body of work, is high-energy and motivational, positioning marketing competence as a learnable, non-negotiable skill for any small-business owner who wants to grow rather than plateau.
keyLessons: Most plateaued businesses have a marketing problem, not a product-quality problem, according to the book's core framing.
Many business owners are still applying marketing assumptions from an earlier commercial era that no longer match how customers actually find and evaluate businesses.
Publishing a book is presented as a high-leverage marketing and branding asset, creating credibility and differentiation that generic advertising doesn't.
A book-as-marketing-asset works as ongoing, largely passive lead generation and credibility-building once created, rather than one-off advertising spend.
Differentiating on expertise and authority is framed as more sustainable than competing purely on price.
Marketing is treated as a learnable, non-negotiable business skill, not something to outsource entirely or ignore in favor of focusing only on the product/service itself.
whoThisIsFor: Small-business owners and service providers who are confident in their core offering but struggling with visibility or lead generation, particularly those open to authorship as a growth strategy.
whenToReadThis: When a business has plateaued despite a genuinely good product or service, and marketing/visibility is the more likely bottleneck than delivery quality.

authorBio.name: Gerry Robert
authorBio.bio:
Gerry Robert is a Canadian-born author, speaker, and publisher who, after an earlier career including theological training and pastoral work, moved into business coaching and motivational speaking, eventually building a reputation around entrepreneurial marketing and personal-development content. His earlier book, *The Millionaire Mindset*, was an international bestseller and established much of his public platform.

He later founded a publishing company (Black Card Books) specifically oriented around helping entrepreneurs and experts use authorship as a business and marketing tool, a focus that directly informs the core strategy emphasized in *Multiply Your Business*. He continues to work as a speaker and consultant internationally, particularly across Asia-Pacific markets.

conceptsFrameworks.name: The Book-as-Marketing-Asset Strategy
conceptsFrameworks.definition: Gerry Robert's recurring, career-defining strategy of using authorship — writing and publishing a book related to one's business or expertise — as a marketing and branding tool that builds credibility, differentiates from competitors, and generates inbound interest in a way that's harder to replicate through conventional advertising.
conceptsFrameworks.sourceSection: (thematic — confirmed via multiple review sources rather than a specific chapter)

actionSteps: Outline a short book, guide, or in-depth resource related to your business's expertise that you could realistically publish within the next year as a credibility and marketing asset.
Audit your current marketing for assumptions that may be outdated (e.g., relying only on traditional advertising or referrals) versus current customer discovery patterns.
List one way you currently compete primarily on price, and brainstorm one way to differentiate instead on demonstrated expertise or authority.
reflectionQuestions: Is your business's growth plateau more likely a marketing visibility problem or a genuine product/service problem — and how would you actually test which one it is?
What would publishing a book or in-depth guide related to your expertise realistically change about how prospective customers perceive you?

points: I could not verify a specific, edition-confirmed list of the book's "10" versus "12" marketing realities (different editions/subtitles exist), which limits how specific and checkable a critique of its individual claims can be — this itself is worth noting as a real weakness in the book's public documentation/consistency across editions.

The book-as-marketing-asset strategy, while genuinely useful for building authority, is also Gerry Robert's own core commercial offering (through his publishing company), which is worth factoring in as a potential conflict of interest when evaluating how strongly the book pushes that particular tactic relative to alternatives.

General marketing advice books in this genre often understate the ongoing effort required to make a published book actually generate leads (distribution, promotion, follow-up systems), rather than treating publication itself as sufficient.
